column5: Collagen is the main structural protein found in our body's connective tissue (skin, joints, bones, hair, nails, muscles, and tendons). It supports beauty, skin elasticity and hydration, joint mobility, bones, muscles, and general health of the connective tissue. HealthAid Marine Collagen Powder is rich in type 1 as well as type 2 and 3 Collagen. It is Hydrolysed to reduce the size of the Collagen molecules thus ensuring better absorption and bioavailability. Supplementing with natural collagen is essential for maintaining healthy-looking skin and joint mobility. The skin is the body’s largest organ and Collagen is the major structural protein of the skin, which gives it strength, smooth and glowing appearance. As we age, Collagen levels decline, and levels of free radicals in the skin increase due to the effects of exposure to harmful UV rays and environmental factors. Cosmetic creams, lotions and serums work on the top layer of skin – the epidermis. However, the skin’s overall quality, moisture-retaining ability and resilience are determined in the deeper, structural layer - the dermis – where the collagen, elastin and moisture-retaining elements are found. Hydrolysed Marine Collagen Powder acts as a skin rejuvenator from inside out because it is especially rich in the beneficial Type I Hydrolysed Collagen to provide the optimum support for healthy, glowing skin. Type I Hydrolysed Collagen is the most abundant in the body and is considered to be the key building matrix protein that gives the skin its structure and firmness. Being “hydrolysed” it has higher bioavailability (90-95%) and can be easily absorbed and transported to the dermis of the skin.

column5: Bio-Folate tablets contain L-methylfolate (5-MTHF) which is a superior alternative to Folic Acid as it is a stable, safe and highly biologically active form of Folate (Vitamin B9). Unlike Folic Acid, L-methylfolate doesn’t require an enzyme for its conversion. For this reason, L-methylfolate is the best option particularly for those with MTHFR mutation, as they can’t metabolise Folic Acid. Folate is a member of the B group vitamins. It plays an important role in normal blood formation and amino acid synthesis. It contributes to the reduction of tiredness and fatigue, homocysteine metabolism, immune and psychological function, and normal maternal tissue growth during pregnancy. Deficiency of Folate leads to fatigue and tiredness, anaemia (usually combined with B12 deficiency), painful mouth sores, poor memory and focus, low mood, depression, insomnia, and dark skin spots. Increased risk of birth defects is also linked to the deficiency of Folate (as well as vitamin B12). For this reason, the Government’s Chief Medical Officer advises that all women planning a pregnancy should take 400?g of supplemental Folate daily from start of trying to conceive until the 12th week of pregnancy. Vitamin B9 (Folate) contributes to the maintenance of healthy heart function, normal blood pressure, blood cholesterol and glucose levels. Scientific research has demonstrated strong evidence that Folate when paired with Vitamin B12 can effectively keep blood homocysteine levels under control. Homocysteine is a type of amino acid that can contribute to the formation of blood clots and cause arteries to narrow and harden. L-methylfolate and Folic Acid supplements should be taken with 1000mcg of Vitamin B12 to prevent B12 deficiency.

column5: Vitamin D is a fat-soluble vitamin, which can be created by the body when the skin is exposed to sunshine for a small amount of time. Certain factors such as the amount of melanin found in your skin, limited sun exposure and lack of Vitamin D in foods can deplete Vitamin D stored within the body over time. A lack of Vitamin D can lead to symptoms such as lethargy, tiredness, muscle problems, bone pains and mood changes. Vitamin D is also used within the body to maintain the normal functioning of the immune system, cell division, and helps maintain normal muscle function.

column5: Gout is an arthritic condition that is an inflammation of one or more joints in the body caused by a build-up of uric acid. Uric acid is a normal by-product of purine breakdown in the body, which is usually removed from the blood by the kidneys and excreted with urine. If too much uric acid is produced or not filtered adequately and excreted, then uric acid can build up and form tiny crystals in and around joint tissues. When these crystals are released into joint space it usually causes pain and inflammation in the body. column5: Vitamin D is a fat-soluble vitamin, which can be created by the body when the skin is exposed to sunshine for a small amount of time. Certain factors such as the amount of melanin found in your skin, limited sun exposure and lack of Vitamin D in foods can deplete Vitamin D stored within the body over time. A lack of Vitamin D can lead to symptoms such as lethargy, tiredness, muscle problems, bone pains and mood changes. Vitamin D is important for a range of bodily functions, and supplementation alongside a healthy diet can contribute to the normal absorption and utilisation of Calcium and Phosphorus, which is important for the maintenance of normal bones and teeth. Vitamin D is also used within the body to maintain the normal functioning of the immune system, cell division, and helps maintain normal muscle function.

column5: Vitamin D is a fat-soluble vitamin, which can be created by the body when the skin is exposed to sunshine for a small amount of time. Certain factors such as the amount of melanin found in your skin, limited sun exposure and lack of Vitamin D in foods can deplete Vitamin D stored within the body over time. A lack of Vitamin D can lead to symptoms such as lethargy, tiredness, muscle problems, bone pains and mood changes. Vitamin D is important for a range of bodily functions, and supplementation alongside a healthy diet can contribute to the normal absorption and utilisation of Calcium and Phosphorus, which is important for the maintenance of normal bones and teeth. Vitamin D is also used within the body to maintain the normal functioning of the immune system, cell division, and helps maintain normal muscle function.

column5: Zinc deficiency affects about 1 in 3 people worldwide. Signs of Zinc deficiency include wounds that take time to heal, trouble concentrating, stomach problems, decreased sense of smell and taste, hair loss, loss of appetite and unexplained weight loss. Fertility problems can be exacerbated by a lack of sufficient Zinc. Recurring health problems related to a low immune system could also be an indication of Zinc deficiency. Zinc in the form of Zinc Gluconate contains 10mg of elemental Zinc which is easily assimilated in the body. Zinc is involved in a great number of biological functions. It aids normal cell division, which makes it especially important for growth and development during pregnancy and childhood. It is involved in bone formation and mineralisation, helping to maintain strong bones and teeth. Zinc also plays an important role in collagen and protein synthesis, vision, sexual function, fertility, antioxidant activity, immunity and much more.

column5: Cholesterol is a naturally occurring fat-like substance that the body needs to function optimally. Within the body, there are different types of cholesterol, some are beneficial and others harmful for the body. The harmful type, known as Low-Density Lipoproteins (LDL Cholesterol) or bad cholesterol, can lead to artery blockages and potentially severe heart conditions. LDL Cholesterol tends to accumulate and create plaque in artery walls. On the other hand, the beneficial type, called High-Density Lipoproteins (HDL Cholesterol), helps manage the levels of bad cholesterol in the bloodstream. Certain nutrients and plant extracts are beneficial in the balance of good cholesterol and bad cholesterol. column5: We’ve all heard how carrots are good for your eyesight, but how? All because of a special Phyto-nutrient called Beta-Carotene, which is abundant in certain fruits and vegetables. Yellow and orange fruits and vegetables get their colour because of their Beta-Carotene content. It is important to incorporate foods with different colours onto our diet. The body converts Beta Carotene into Vitamin A, which contributes to the maintenance of good eyesight, a healthy immune system and normal metabolism. Beta Carotene is a safe and effective way of taking Vitamin A, as the body only converts the required amount into Vitamin A. HealthAid® has created a mixed Carotenoid capsule for your body to convert into its own Vitamin A to use as it needs, without the risk of excess Vitamin A ingestion. HealthAid® Beta Carotene Capsules contain natural Beta Carotene derived from the sea plant Dunaliecia Salina, found in the unpolluted lake of Whyalla in South Australia.

column5: Carboslim® Capsules have been designed to assist those on a low carbohydrate weight management programme. The other function of this key ingredient is to obstruct the dietary breakdown of starches into glucose, allowing carbohydrates to pass through the system unchanged. Carboslim® Capsules also contain Chromium and Green Tea Extract to assist in the support of a low carbohydrate diet by burning up fat, improving metabolism and increasing energy levels. The optimum time to take Carboslim® Capsule is just before a starch–rich meal along with a full glass of water, however, Carboslim® could still provide some of its starch neutralising benefits when taken during, or just after, a starch-rich meal.

column5: Creatine is a natural energy source that is used in muscle and nerve tissue. Creatine is stored as Creatine phosphate (phosphocreatine) in muscle cells. This phosphocreatine is the important factor that forms ATP (Adenosine Tri Phosphate), one of the body’s quick energy molecules. Creatine replaces the ATP that has been used up during muscle contraction to allow prolonged intense activity. Creatine Monohydrate supplementation increases phosphocreatine levels in the muscle, especially when accompanied by exercise or carbohydrate intake, therefore forming an effective energy transfer system across cells. It may increase muscle gain and lean body mass. People who are involved in intense physical activity or limit their intake of animal products may be well advised to include HealthAid® Creatine Monohydrate powder in their diet. This may help increase the muscle stores of Creatine needed in weight lifting or sprinting.

column5: Vitamin D is a fat-soluble vitamin, which can be created by the body when the skin is exposed to sunshine for a small amount of time. Certain factors such as the amount of melanin found in your skin, limited sun exposure and lack of Vitamin D in foods can deplete Vitamin D stored within the body over time. A lack of Vitamin D can lead to symptoms such as lethargy, tiredness, muscle problems, bone pains and mood changes. Vitamin D is important for a range of bodily functions, and supplementation alongside a healthy diet can contribute to the normal absorption and utilisation of Calcium and Phosphorus, which is important for the maintenance of normal bones and teeth. Vitamin D is also used within the body to maintain the normal functioning of the immune system, cell division, and helps maintain normal muscle function.

column5: Vitamin D is a fat-soluble vitamin, which can be created by the body when the skin is exposed to sunshine for a small amount of time. Certain factors such as the amount of melanin found in your skin, limited sun exposure and lack of Vitamin D in foods can deplete Vitamin D stored within the body over time. A lack of Vitamin D can lead to symptoms such as lethargy, tiredness, muscle problems, bone pains and mood changes. Vitamin D is important for a range of bodily functions, and supplementation alongside a healthy diet can contribute to the normal absorption and utilisation of Calcium and Phosphorus, which is important for the maintenance of normal bones and teeth. Vitamin D is also used within the body to maintain the normal functioning of the immune system, cell division, and helps maintain normal muscle function. column5: Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is often referred to as the energy currency of life because the amount that we have in our tissues determines how much energy we have. It is needed to help our hearts and muscles to contract. Brain requires it to perform its cognitive functions fluently. It is also involved in countless other actions that we don’t consciously control. D-Ribose is the key building block of ATP, therefore the availability of D-Ribose is vital for energy production and recovery. When the cells in muscles such as the heart come under metabolic stress, they are unable to synthesise enough D-Ribose and as a result, energy levels are depleted.

column5: Methylcobalamin is regarded as the final and most bio-available form of Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin). Unfortunately, due to many different factors, Vitamin B12 deficiency is a common and growing problem today. It is common for individuals to have signs of a Vitamin B12 deficiency without even knowing. A deficiency may show signs such as mental fogginess, poor memory and concentration, fatigue, irritation, lack of motivation, mood swings, muscle weakness and sleeping problems. Lack of this Vitamin may also contribute to weakened immunity. Vitamin B12 is important for good mental and physical health. It contributes to normal brain functionality, immune system function, energy production, and the metabolism of fats, carbohydrates and proteins. It supports the heart and cardiovascular system by maintaining normal homocysteine levels.

column5: 5-HTP (5-Hydroxytryptophan) is derived from the seeds of the Griffonia simplicifolia plant. 5-HTP is a naturally occurring Amino Acid that aids the production of the important brain neurotransmitter, Serotonin. Serotonin is involved in mood and emotion regulation, behaviour patterns, appetite control, and sleep mechanisms. Tryptophan is obtained from the diet and converted into 5HTP within the body. 5-HTP is able to cross the blood-brain barrier, where it is transformed into Serotonin. 5-HTP is commonly used to support cognitive function by managing mental health (stress and symptoms of depression and anxiety), sleeping patterns, fibromyalgia and migraine relief.
